key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method can model ductile fracture by coupling J2 plasticity and phase-field fracture with separate neural representations for displacement and crack phase.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-informed, mesh-free alternative for predicting elastic-plastic damage and crack growth in ductile solids with good agreement to finite-element references.
method: Uses small-strain J2 plasticity with linear isotropic hardening and a second-order Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture model.
Represents displacement with a ReZero residual neural network and the phase field with localized Gaussian radial basis functions.
Minimizes reduced energy alternately across loading increments, with radial return updates and transfer learning for history variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with finite-element solutions for force-displacement response, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to the loading increment size near abrupt fracture events, so incremental step control is important.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
